proof:
Notation. ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) = Rn d with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩; L(E, F) := E →L[ℝ] F and L(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ, a ring whose multiplication is composition (f * g = f ∘L g holds by rfl) with identity 1; for A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A, so ⟨A* z, c⟩ = ⟨z, A c⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) and ⟨c, A* z⟩ = ⟨A c, z⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right); G := A* ∘L A and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G; trace means LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ applied to the underlying linear map (.toLinearMap); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ (= EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ l). Every lemma cited below resolves after `import GMT.Ch02.Submission` (checked with #check).
Source: parent proof, steps 1 and 7 (J = √det G is C¹ on V and D_vJ = J · trace(G⁻¹ A* S(v,·))).
Setting. A(x) := fderiv ℝ ψ x, A(x)* := adjoint A(x), G(x) := A(x)* ∘L A(x) ∈ L(ℝⁿ), J := Chapter02.areaJacobianAt ψ; for fixed x put S_v := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x v ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G(x). Let adjR : L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) →L[ℝ] L(ℝᴺ, ℝⁿ) be (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (𝕜 := ℝ)).toContinuousLinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearMap; over ℝ the conjugation is trivial, so this is an ℝ-linear continuous map and adjR L = L* holds by rfl.
1. (J = √(det ∘ G).) For every x, J x = √(det G(x)) (Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp), (J x)² = det G(x) (Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_sq_eq_det_adjoint_comp) and J x ≥ 0 (Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_nonneg). So J = fun x ↦ √(det G(x)).
2. (Positivity and Gram facts on V.) For x ∈ V, A(x) is injective, so J x = normDet A(x) ≠ 0 (Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet and LinearMap.normDet_ne_zero_tfae, items 5 ⇒ 1: injective ⇒ normDet ≠ 0); hence J x > 0 and det G(x) = (J x)² > 0. By the sibling gram_projection (K := range A(x)), G(x) is a unit of L(ℝⁿ) and G⁻¹ is symmetric: ⟨G⁻¹v, w⟩ = ⟨v, G⁻¹w⟩.
3. (Regularity and derivative of G.) V is open and ψ is C² on V, so A = fderiv ℝ ψ is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen, 1 + 1 ≤ 2); at x ∈ V it is differentiable with derivative v ↦ S_v. Hence x ↦ A(x)* = adjR (A x) is C¹ on V, with derivative adjR ∘L (v ↦ S_v), i.e. v ↦ S_v*, at x (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff, chain rule). Composition is continuous bilinear, so G = A* ∘L A is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.clm_comp), and by the product rule fderiv_clm_comp, DG(x)[v] = A(x)* ∘L S_v + S_v* ∘L A(x).
4. (Derivative of det ∘ G.) By the sibling det_jacobi, det is C¹ (so differentiable at G(x)) and, G(x) being a unit, D det(G(x))[H] = det G(x) · trace(G⁻¹ ∘L H). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp), det ∘ G is differentiable at x ∈ V with D(det ∘ G)(x)[v] = det G(x) · trace(G⁻¹ ∘L (A* ∘L S_v + S_v* ∘L A)) = det G(x) · (trace(G⁻¹A*S_v) + trace(G⁻¹S_v*A)) (ContinuousLinearMap.comp_add, linearity of trace).
5. (The two traces agree.) In the orthonormal basis (e_l) (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner), for each l, using symmetry of G⁻¹, adjoint_inner_right, adjoint_inner_left and real_inner_comm:
   ⟨e_l, G⁻¹(S_v*(A e_l))⟩ = ⟨G⁻¹e_l, S_v*(A e_l)⟩ = ⟨S_v(G⁻¹e_l), A e_l⟩ = ⟨A*(S_v(G⁻¹e_l)), e_l⟩ = ⟨e_l, A*(S_v(G⁻¹e_l))⟩.
   Summing over l: trace(G⁻¹ ∘ S_v* ∘ A) = trace((A* ∘ S_v) ∘ G⁻¹), and by cyclicity (LinearMap.trace_comp_comm') trace((A* ∘ S_v) ∘ G⁻¹) = trace(G⁻¹ ∘ A* ∘ S_v). (The equality holds only after summation, not term by term.) Hence D(det ∘ G)(x)[v] = 2 det G(x) · trace(G⁻¹ ∘L A(x)* ∘L S_v).
6. (First conjunct.) For x ∈ V, det ∘ G is C¹ at x (V is a neighbourhood of x; det C¹ by det_jacobi, G C¹ by step 3) and det G(x) ≠ 0 (step 2), so x′ ↦ √(det G(x′)) is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.sqrt). By step 1, J is C¹ on V.
7. (Second conjunct.) For x ∈ V, HasFDerivAt.sqrt (det G(x) ≠ 0) shows that J = √(det ∘ G) has derivative (1/(2√(det G(x)))) • D(det ∘ G)(x) at x. With √(det G(x)) = J x, det G(x) = (J x)² and J x > 0, step 5 gives fderiv ℝ J x v = (1/(2 J x)) · 2 (J x)² · trace(G⁻¹A*S_v) = J x · trace(G⁻¹ ∘L A(x)* ∘L S_v), i.e. fderiv ℝ (areaJacobianAt ψ) x v = areaJacobianAt ψ x * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Rn n) (Ring.inverse (A(x)* ∘L A(x)) ∘L A(x)* ∘L fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x v).toLinearMap. (For n = 0 every trace on ℝ⁰ vanishes and J ≡ 1; the argument covers this.) ∎
key_steps: J = √(det ∘ G) everywhere; on V, A injective ⇒ J > 0 and det G = J² > 0; G(x) is a unit with symmetric inverse (gram_projection).
A = fderiv ψ is C¹ on V; with the ℝ-linear adjoint adjR, G = A*A is C¹ and DG(x)[v] = A*S_v + S_v*A (fderiv_clm_comp).
det_jacobi + chain rule: D(det∘G)(x)[v] = det G · (trace(G⁻¹A*S_v) + trace(G⁻¹S_v*A)), and the basis-sum/cyclicity argument gives trace(G⁻¹S_v*A) = trace(G⁻¹A*S_v).
ContDiffAt.sqrt / HasFDerivAt.sqrt: J is C¹ on V and DJ(x)[v] = (2 det G trace(G⁻¹A*S_v))/(2J) = J trace(G⁻¹A*S_v).
